claims.implementation: lifecycle.recovery/recovery_supervisor.py's RecoverySupervisor is the sole production caller of ROLLBACK_STABLE (check_repository_structure.py check 11 confines Stable-mutation write capability to this context). It imports no AI provider, no candidate-generation authority and no repair pipeline - only the PDP grant (via RollbackAuthorization), the Package-1 Stable-revision pointer, and the C-14/C-15 evidence plane (via EvidenceSink).

pdp.py's fixed rule for ROLLBACK_STABLE (RECOVERY_SUPERVISOR_ONLY) is the sole path by which any actor may mutate the Stable revision pointer; WRITE_STABLE_FILE remains DENY for every actor unconditionally, untouched by this phase.

pdp.py::_rollback_rule denies ROLLBACK_STABLE to every actor except the canonical invoker read from AUTHORITY_MAP.yaml (lifecycle.recovery), never hard-coded, and the grant cannot be forged by stating the verified fact as any other actor.

lifecycle.release/stable_pointer.py's StableRevisionPointer.is_previously_verified(revision_id) is the whole of what a 'previously verified immutable revision' means: membership in the pointer's own durable history, built only from genuine StableCandidatePath.promotion_receipt proofs (the full canonical stable->candidate->verification->acceptance->promotion path) - never a caller's bare assertion.
claims.evidence: backend/tests/persistence/test_stable_pointer.py::TestPromotion and TestRollback (promotion requires the full receipt; rollback refuses any target the pointer never recorded) and test_phase_22b_journey.py::TestWrongCandidateAndCorruptedTargetRefusal (denied twice over: real PDP and the pointer's own defence-in-depth check)

claims.implementation: StableRevisionPointer serialises its whole state once and swaps it into place with a single os.replace, so a reader never observes a partially written pointer; the abandoned current revision joins history rather than being discarded on every switch (promote or rollback_to).

rollback_to is an identity-only pointer switch (no content read, generated or transformed); RecoverySupervisor imports no AI provider and no candidate-generation authority; every rollback target must already be pointer-recorded (no unverified target); evidence is always emitted (no bypass); the rollback record itself states 'transformation: none'.
claims.evidence: backend/tests/persistence/test_phase_22b_journey.py::TestNoNovelContentNoAIInvocation (structural scans plus the real persisted artifact payload asserting its own transformation field) and TestWrongCandidateAndCorruptedTargetRefusal (unverified-target refusal)

claims.implementation: RecoverySupervisor.rollback always registers a real C-14 artifact describing the rollback and appends a real C-15 evidence row against it for ARK-REQ-0160 itself, via the EvidenceSink Protocol adapting evidence.audit.AuditChain unmodified.
claims.evidence: backend/tests/persistence/test_recovery_supervisor.py::TestGenuineRollback::test_evidence_is_really_persisted_and_chain_intact (3 real persisted, chain-intact evidence rows, re-read from a fresh session) and test_phase_22b_journey.py::TestTheComposedVDCSequence

claims.implementation: The composed VDC 'Recovery Supervisor' sequence (bad candidate -> launch -> health failure -> known-good rollback -> failure record -> stable available) runs end to end on real SQLite (via the real Alembic chain), the real PDP, the real Stable-revision pointer and the real C-14/C-15 evidence plane, and the run itself is what RecoverySupervisor.is_verified() detects.

rollback_to switches the pointer's current revision to a target StableRevisionPointer.is_previously_verified confirms was itself previously verified through the canonical promotion path, performing no content transformation - the registered rollback artifact records this explicitly.
